newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks hit fourth record closing this year.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks hit fourth record closing this year.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE
NIKKEI 18090.04 -54.30 LME CASH NICKEL US$7245 +110.0
CANDLR 1.3408 LME CASH ALUM US$1583.0 -4.0
CAN 30-YR 108.40 +0.40 FEB BRENT CRUDE US$22.53 -0.53
* Toronto stocks climb 35 points to this year's fourth closing high and hit new intra-day record. * Key index in seven day winning streak, aided by stronger golds, conglomerates.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key index turned in another solid performance on Friday, posting a fourth record close for 1997 and hitting a new intra-day high as well.
The TSE 300 Composite Index added 35.14 points to close at 6138.80 in a seven session winning streak. Trading again was brisk: 120.3 million shares moved worth C$1.85 billion.
The new lifetime high is now 6144.29 points.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, all but three -- real estate, forestry products and utilities -- climbed. Consumer products, golds, conglomerates and media stocks surged the most.
"Stocks are terrific. Another up day, in Toronto, across the board," said Maison Placements Canada president John Ing. "Gold stocks were very strong."
Bullion prices managed to push heavily weighted golds higher. Comex February gold rose $1.40 to finish at $356.40 on Friday.

Toronto's market has also benefitted from a recent influx of cash as Canadians turn some bank savings into tax sheltered pension funds ahead of an end-February deadline for 1996 retirement plans, analysts said.
Advancers outpaced decliners 603 to 430 while 263 traded unchanged.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Penny stock Mineral Resources Corp topped Toronto's most actives. Shares rose a cent to seven and a half cents after news it plans a takeover bid for ailing miner Anvil Range Mining Corp.
* Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd jumped 1.25 to 25.30 on nearly 3.5 million shares, helped by stronger energy prices.
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd slipped 0.30 to 24.40. It said it was reviewing the Placer Dome Inc offer.
